_readme: benarbejde/asset_manifest.json -- Example Music Limited -- fetch-on-demand manifest for
bootstrap/web/ boot assets that have a real upstream, instead of vendoring them into git.
Consumed by bootstrap/setup-workstation-linux.sh, bootstrap/setup-workstation-macos.sh, and
bootstrap/Setup-Workstation.ps1. Every dest path is relative to bootstrap/web/. Nothing in
here is auto-run by the harness (at_have_ryggen_fri/check_bootstrap_assets.py stays
read-only, offline) -- fetching is always an explicit, separate script run.
Arch Linux, Rocky Linux, and Ubuntu (Alpine dd-writer) menu.ipxe entries were removed
entirely 2026-07-27 (Robert's call) -- none had real working assets (Ubuntu/Rocky had none
committed at all; Arch's own airootfs.sfs/initramfs-linux were literal placeholder stub
files, not real assets). See menu.ipxe's own v2.10 changelog entry.
The WinPE .wim is deliberately NOT here and NEVER goes in this repo at all, LFS or
otherwise -- this repo cannot redistribute it (Microsoft ADK licensing). wimboot (the loader
that streams it, github.com/ipxe/wimboot) IS fetched below -- it's GPL2, no Microsoft code
in it, unaffected. See .gitignore's matching hard exclusion.
source_type github_release: queries the GitHub Releases API fresh every run and uses the
API's own per-asset 'digest' field for checksum verification -- nothing hardcoded here to go
stale. tag 'latest' always takes whatever's newest; a literal tag (e.g. 'v2.9.0') pins to
that exact release.
source_type url_with_checksum_file: fetches checksum_file_url as text, finds the line
containing checksum_file_entry, and regex-extracts a 64-hex-char SHA256 substring from it --
format-agnostic on purpose, so it doesn't matter whether the upstream checksum file uses GNU
style ('<hash>  <path>', Debian's SHA256SUMS) or BSD style ('SHA256 (<file>) = <hash>',
OpenBSD's SHA256).
archives[]: one download serves multiple destination files via members[] -- fetched once,
not once per member. checksum_file_url/checksum_file_entry are OPTIONAL on an archives[]
entry (added 2026-07-27 for the hdt/ entry below, same format-agnostic extraction as
url_with_checksum_file) -- omit both to skip verification, as gparted's entry below still
does (pre-existing gap, not fixed in this pass: SourceForge doesn't publish a convenient
checksum file for gparted-live the way kernel.org does for syslinux).
archives[] supports .zip extraction (unzip / Expand-Archive) and, added 2026-08-13, .iso
extraction (7z on Linux/macOS; Mount-DiskImage, native, on Windows -- no extra dependency
there). Prefer a .zip release over .tar.xz/.tar.gz where the upstream offers a choice, rather
than adding tar support to all 3 platform scripts for one entry.
--refresh: all 3 setup scripts now accept this flag, which forces every assets[]/archives[]
entry to re-fetch even if its dest file(s) already exist (workstation_tools[] already always
re-checks its own checksum every run regardless, so --refresh changes nothing there). Default
behaviour unchanged -- skip-if-already-present, same as before.
GParted Live is x86_64 only -- it has never published an arm64 build.
workstation_tools[]: a SEPARATE category from assets[]/archives[] above -- these are real
locally-run tools installed onto an engineer's own machine (alongside install_deps()'s
apt/brew/choco packages in each setup script), not boot assets served from bootstrap/web/.
Each entry is pinned to an exact tag (never 'latest' -- Robert's own tool, reproducible
builds matter more here than always grabbing newest), with a per-platform asset_name map
keyed 'goos-goarch' (matches Go's own GOOS/GOARCH naming, which is how fyrtaarn's own release
pipeline names its build artifacts). Checksum verification uses the same GitHub Releases API
'digest' field as assets[]'s github_release handling -- nothing hardcoded to go stale.
check_workstation_tool_versions.py (at_have_ryggen_fri/) checks the pinned tag against the
real upstream 'latest' release and flags drift -- informational, since bumping the pin is a
deliberate human decision (a new release might need testing before every engineer's machine
picks it up), not something to silently auto-adopt.
Changelog:
2026-08-13  Robert's idea: replaced the 4 debian/trixie/*/{ linux, initrd.gz } per-file
url_with_checksum_file entries with 4 archives[] entries that extract both from
the upstream mini.iso instead (bookworm+trixie x86_64+arm64). The old approach
fetched linux/initrd.gz independently, which could fall out of version-sync with
each other -- a real live kernel/initrd mismatch had already been worked around by
hand once. mini.iso ships both from the same debian-cd build, coherently versioned
by construction, closing the gap at the root instead of re-fetching by hand after
each Debian point release. Verified live before writing these entries: downloaded
the real trixie/amd64 mini.iso, confirmed /linux and /initrd.gz sit at the ISO
root (no subdirectory), and that both are byte-identical to what was already
hand-placed on disk. Also gave bookworm/'s files (hand-placed, never in this
manifest before) their first real manifest coverage.
2026-07-27  Migrated from asset_manifest.yml (same schema, same verified URLs/tags/paths --
see project memory for the research trail). JSON instead of YAML so this parses
natively in bash (jq) and PowerShell (ConvertFrom-Json) without an extra
dependency -- ansible/playbooks/bootstrap_assets/fetch-assets.yml (the Ansible
playbook this replaces) is being retired since ansible-playbook cannot run
natively on Windows at all.
2026-07-27  Moved from bootstrap/asset_manifest.json to benarbejde/asset_manifest.json --
Robert's call: this is raw source-of-truth data, belongs alongside
benarbejde/'s other JSON files (ad_forest.json, address_policy.json, etc.), not
off in bootstrap/ where nothing else JSON-shaped lives. The consuming scripts
(bootstrap/setup-workstation-{linux,macos}.sh,
bootstrap/Setup-Workstation.ps1) stay in bootstrap/ -- only the data moved.
2026-07-27  Added the hdt/ archive entry (SYSLINUX 6.03 -- lpxelinux.0, hdt.c32,
libcom32.c32, libutil.c32) and dropped the earlier note about rockylinux/ being
deferred -- Rocky Linux's menu.ipxe entries were removed entirely, not deferred.
Arch/Rocky/Ubuntu removal itself needed no manifest changes -- none of those had
manifest entries (Arch = custom build, Rocky/Ubuntu = never had a fetch source).
2026-08-06  klargoring entries reworked for arm64 (PVE 9.2's own arm64 release, Robert --
https://pve.proxmox.com/wiki/Roadmap). The real upstream release
(github.com/knightmare2600/klargoring, checked live: klargoring-20260806-
trixie-4) publishes vmlinuz-amd64/vmlinuz-arm64 etc, not the old unsuffixed
'vmlinuz' this manifest previously pointed at -- that asset name no longer
exists upstream at all, so the pre-existing amd64 entries were already stale,
not just missing arm64 coverage. dest paths now match menu.ipxe v2.11's
klargoring/amd64/ + klargoring/arm64/ split. Added KERNEL_VERSION-{amd64,arm64}
too (not consumed by any code, but a real published release asset worth
keeping fetchable alongside its vmlinuz/initrd).
2026-08-08  Added workstation_tools[] (new category, see _readme note above) with fyrtaarn
(github.com/knightmare2600/fyrtaarn, Robert's own BMC controller app) -- pinned
0.0.7.8, checked live against the real release (10 platform binaries + a
SHA256SUMS.txt, all digests cross-verified against the GitHub API's own per-asset
digest field before this entry was written). Robert: 'use that inside of those
deployment scripts we wrote, and also have the harness check for new versions,
verify checksums, all the usual spangly stuff.'

archives._comment: Debian netboot mini.iso, x86_64. Replaces the old per-file linux/initrd.gz url_with_checksum_file entries (removed 2026-08-13) -- those were fetched independently and could genuinely fall out of version-sync with each other (the real cause of a live kernel/initrd mismatch, worked around by hand at the time). mini.iso ships both in one Debian-built, coherently-versioned image -- extract from it instead, same debian-cd build, same guarantee they match. Verified live 2026-08-13: extracted /linux and /initrd.gz from a real downloaded mini.iso, byte-identical to what was already hand-placed on disk. 'stable' in the URL (not 'trixie') matches the existing convention already used by klargoring/openbsd entries above -- Debian's own alias for whatever the current stable release is; dest stays 'trixie' since that's the current stable codename, same gap as before if/when the next stable release ships (not fixed in this pass).
Debian netboot mini.iso, arm64 -- same reasoning as the x86_64 entry above.
Debian netboot mini.iso, bookworm x86_64 -- bookworm/'s files existed on disk before this manifest tracked them at all (hand-placed); this is the first manifest coverage they've ever had.
Debian netboot mini.iso, bookworm arm64 -- same reasoning as the bookworm x86_64 entry above.

SYSLINUX 6.03 (last stable release) -- pxelinux.0's own follow-up fetches (config, .c32 modules) expect TFTP; lpxelinux.0 is SYSLINUX's HTTP-native build, matching this repo's HTTP-only web server. x86_64/BIOS only -- HDT itself is a legacy BIOS tool, no arm64 build exists. .zip release used (not .tar.xz) so the existing unzip/Expand-Archive extraction path works unmodified across all 3 platform scripts -- confirmed byte-for-byte same file layout as the .tar.xz release, just without the syslinux-6.03/ prefix directory.

workstation_tools.name: fyrtaarn
workstation_tools._comment: Robert's own BMC controller app, self-contained Go binary, no runtime deps. Installed to /usr/local/bin/fyrtaarn (Linux/macOS) or C:\Tools\fyrtaarn\fyrtaarn.exe (Windows, matching this repo's existing C:\Tools\<name>\ convention -- see docs/gitleaks_guide.md). The 3 workstation setup scripts only consume linux-amd64/linux-arm64/darwin-amd64/darwin-arm64/windows-amd64/windows-arm64 -- the remaining entries (armv7, mips64el, mipsel, ppc64) are real published SBC/embedded builds kept here for completeness and for check_workstation_tool_versions.py's own existence/checksum verification, not currently installed by any script.
